title: Normalized continuous rational realization data
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E$ vary over finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], completed continuous coefficient rings [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and cohomology [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and the constructible continuous-module predicate [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. A base consists of a noetherian scheme $X$, a finite dimension bound and stalkwise invertibility of $\ell$. For these bases use the integral constructible-complete subcategory [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], its raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] and localized standard t-structure [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. A normalized realization at $(E,X)$ consists of the continuous coefficient identifications, fixed on continuous functions and every finite residue, an additive $E$-linear triangulated functor $J_X$ into the ambient derived module category, its integral scalar-extension comparison and fractional-map equation, full faithfulness, constructible essential image, both standard degree-bound equivalences, heart identification and the cohomology comparison. Finite locally closed stratifications are those of [def-constructible-stratification]. Define ordinary module inverse image as coefficient extension after site inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and derived module inverse image using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. A pullback datum for $g$ includes its continuous-function coefficient map, finite-residue square, normalized universal derived counit and balanced tensor comparison, preservation by the actual completed pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and its rational comparison normalized by the completion unit. Identity and composition data retain the ordinary tensor units and universal derived counits. Coefficient-change and successive-change data use the actual scalar functors and associators [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], with normalized balanced tensors; mixed data impose their pullback square. Include the exact ordinary inverse-image specializations and site-object restriction using the slice equivalence and continuous-function coefficient identification [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. A realization family is one choice of all these data simultaneously for every finite coefficient field, base, morphism and coefficient embedding, with their identity, composition, successive-extension and mixed equations. This defines data; existence of such a family is a separate theorem.
